key_insight: Informal theorem proving improves when models are trained to recognize and produce concise "insights"—the core techniques or strategies that guide solution construction—bridging the gap between raw LLM output and human-like problem solving.
problem_solved: Addresses the bottleneck that LLMs struggle to identify the key solving technique for complex informal proofs, causing inefficient or incorrect solution attempts and poor generalization.
method: Design a training framework that explicitly models "insight" as an intermediate signal: identify or generate short strategy hints that summarize the core technique for a problem.
Train or fine-tune LLMs to both extract insight from problems and condition proof generation on those insights (supervised and/or self-supervised signal).
Use insight-guided decomposition during generation so proofs follow targeted strategies, improving correctness and interpretability.
impact: Enabling models to reason via explicit insights makes informal theorem proving more accurate, sample-efficient, and interpretable—beneficial for researchers building reasoning-capable LLMs and tools that assist human mathematicians or educators.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Problem → Insight extractor (lightbulb) → Insight-guided proof generator → Final proof
Side-by-side example: same theorem solved without insight (long/incorrect) vs. with insight (compact/correct)
Bar chart showing performance gain (accuracy/solve rate) with insight-guided training vs. baseline
Icon set: lightbulb (insight), puzzle-piece (technique), book/proof (formal result), robot/LLM (model)
paper_title: Learning to Reason with Insight for Informal Theorem Proving
paper_authors: Yunhe Li, Hao Shi, Bowen Deng, Wei Wang, Mengzhe Ruan
